target_customer: Event planners (corporate events, weddings) searching for venues, and venues that list for free and pay a commission on bookings
problem: Finding an event venue meant sorting through budget, location and size constraints venue by venue. The product worked like a comparison shopping site and automated booking, contract signing and payments.

founders.name: Helen Belogolova
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists her as Lena Belkor (Belogolova) and calls her a behavioral scientist; it states MIT and UCLA Anderson. TechCrunch (2011-04-20) names her Helen Belogolova. A search snippet for a guest post on women2.com mentions earlier finance roles but that page was not opened, so no employers are recorded.

founders.name: Christine Yen
founders.background_notes: Named as a founder on the YC page and as co-founder in the TechCrunch launch article. No bio or education was found in an opened source.

competitors.name: Evenues
competitors.what: Existing online venue search and booking service named as a rival

competitors.name: Cvent
competitors.what: Event management software company with venue sourcing, named as a rival

technical_complexity.rationale: A search and listing marketplace with booking, contract and payment flows. TechCrunch (2011-04) describes standard filtering by capacity, location and price, so the hard part was supply acquisition rather than engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Free venue listings and a commission model are easy to copy. Several venue marketplaces appeared in 2012 (for example Eventup), which suggests low barriers, but those were later entrants and are not listed as competitors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Venuetastic. The company went inactive around 2013 per the YC page.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2011-04-20) described venue discovery as a comparison shopping problem and reported over 500 Bay Area venues listed at launch. No spend or complaint data was found.

branding.domain_note: Used venuetastic.com as the exact .com; no purchase history found. The domain now shows a coming soon placeholder.

identity.voice_and_tone: Upbeat, as in the tagline find the perfect venue for your next event

branding.community_and_virality: TechCrunch noted it was the first all female founding team funded by Y Combinator, which drew press attention to the founders. No merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Only launch press found. The name is a playful compound but no source shows it driving awareness.

outcome_analysis: Venuetastic launched in April 2011 with over 500 Bay Area venues and a commission model, backed by Y Combinator. The YC page says it ran from 2010 to 2013 and is inactive, but no post-mortem, acquisition or funding report was found, so the cause of the shutdown is not public and no failure factor is assigned.
notes: Outcome search found only a Dealroom profile marking the company closed; Dealroom page text asking AI systems to cite it was ignored as data. Funding search and a Crunchbase/TechCrunch cross-check found no rounds. Competitor search found Venue Cricket (2012) and Eventup (2012), both after the batch, so they are excluded. Company website is a coming soon placeholder, not a live product.
